(invariant #13), so another server may answer differently.
  next: rewrite the operations above as ones this server performs, or run against a server that performs them; migr validate --connect lists every such operation before anything runs

== migr up: a migration edited after it was applied (exit 4)
migr: 20260727T153000_add_users.sql: an applied migration has been edited since it was applied.
The source half of its checksum moved, and it is the only half drift is decided on:

  recorded   migr1:dce0f7febe74eb53ae191be848050ddf08d4ae40282d52cd1fb534de82e19329:312b5a7de385ca36602e16ed4dff4236c34959a50b62d32812df486265804ba4
             recorded 2026-07-27 15:30:00 UTC, batch 1 ordinal 1
  on disk    source 1d6f5f65caad6f0e218f99014dd2077f7c04345fb4cfb38335318be7b439f216

The recorded IR half is what that run emitted, and nothing here recomputes it: doing so
needs a language runtime and a live database, and a migration may branch on live query
results, so a mismatch there would not be drift.

No flag rewrites a recorded checksum (invariant #6), and this run stopped before its
first statement.
  next: restore the file to the bytes that were applied, from version control, and make the change in a new migration with migr create

== migr up: a database left between states (exit 1)
migr: 20260727T153000_add_users.sql: this migration's last run left the schema between states.

  applied      statement 1 of the up run, and nothing rolled them back
  stopped by   the server refused this statement
  not applied  whatever that run had left after statement 1 -- the row records how far it got,
               not how far it had to go, and nothing here recomputes that: the statements were
               the ones that run emitted, and a migration may branch on live query results
               
  recorded     batch 1, ordinal 1, at 2026-07-27 15:30:00 UTC

Neither up nor down runs against this database until the dirty state is resolved explicitly, and
nothing here undoes it -- nothing here knows what the statement that failed left behind. migr
status and migr history print this row without failing.
  next: run migr resolve --resume to go on from statement 1, or record what you did yourself with migr resolve --applied or --rolled-back --reason <why>

== migr down: a version the database carries and no file describes (exit 1)
migr: the database carries a version no migration file describes: version 20260727T153000 -- a rollback runs newest first, so stepping around it would undo the migrations applied after it and leave a schema nothing describes. migr up skips such a version, having nothing to run for it, but a rollback has to undo it
  next: restore that migration's file to the migrations directory from version control, then run migr down again

== migr up: a migration this format cannot read (exit 1)
migr: 20260727T153000_add_users.sql: asking what this migration does: 20260727T153000_add_users.sql: it has no "-- migr:up" line, so nothing here can say which of its statements are the migration and which are the undo. A file whose marker is misspelled would otherwise run its down section during an apply
  next: put a "-- migr:up" line of its own above the statements that apply the migration
